g.text: Friday 31 July, 08:45. Varma's first question each morning takes the best part of a minute to begin
answering. The second, straight after, starts almost at once.
"Why is it slow only when I arrive?"
Case file 02 chapter 20 found one cause: a timestamp in the system prompt, new every request, so that
nothing after it could be reused.
The cause this morning is the nightly sync. At 01:58 it rewrites the case memory, the second thing
"So every morning it reads everything again from the top," Okafor says.
"From the first thing that changed," you say.
. The same request, and a change at the start, the middle and the end
what is sent, in order (tokens as qwen3 counts the text)
Reading the prompt, qwen3:8b on local Ollama, 3 times each
s. Prompt tokens reported for the same prompt twice were
The morning after the sync: reading the prompt, seconds
. Does the order change the answers?
. On a hosted model: breakpoints and a price calculation
A session of 10 questions on claude-sonnet-5-5: a price calculation from these
cache breakpoints, one at the end of each group but the question. Cached prefix:
everything up to the case memory,
tokens out a question, as step
Prices per million tokens from config.yaml, checked
. Not run on the hosted model: no key.
On qwen3:8b on local Ollama, reading this 5,410-token context took 23.78 s the first time and 0.05 s the
same again (medians of 3). A change at the end cost 0.34 s, in the middle 12.69 s, at the start 23.76 s:
the server reads again from the first thing that changed, and reports the same token count either way.
On the morning after the sync, today's order made the first question read 4,576 tokens again (19.60 s);
with what changes least first it was 1,150 (5.88 s), 70% less time. The new order scored 16 of 26
against 17, with 0 fixed and 1 broken. On the hosted model the same layout carries 4 cache breakpoints;
its price is calculated here, not measured.
